introduction: Follow the fallen priest’s scroll exchange and explore Mir’s webbed forest, stranded travelers, river, hidden lairs, wyrms, relics and rune-covered stone.
orientation: Enter the Forest of Mir from the desert road or follow the river into the forest. Arriving discovers the zone; meeting the fallen priest reveals his request.
Ask the fallen priest about hello or greetings. Both words share his request for a scroll with powers of good and evil gods.

Bring one light and dark scroll to the priest for experience and a satanic token. The male thorny worm carries the source scroll in a hidden dark hole. An exact supplied scroll also fits; a remembered personal kill, first recovery or greeting is not required.

Carry the scroll loose before offering it. The optional preparation row shows current loose custody. A held, worn or packed scroll needs different offering preparation; possessing it does not prove its origin or an accepted exchange.
Offer the exact loose scroll to the priest. One accepted exchange records completion. A spent scroll, a missing token, a creature defeat or a room visit cannot replace or erase that history.
The light and dark scroll can also be recited for its own spells. Using a scroll and offering it to the priest are different choices. The vellum map carried by Johan is a different item.

Johan, Mythra, the Xort beast and the orc warband suggest other forest stories. Their equipment, descriptive injuries or a fallen creature do not prove that someone was helped or that a threat was resolved.
Tall trees offer viewpoints and clues about the forest. A refuge description does not promise safety. Discovering a landmark, finding a way out and safely guiding someone are different outcomes.

The river can carry travelers along its bends. Traveling against the current, drifting, landing safely and helping another traveler are separate results; the pleasant-current description does not remove the water hazards.

A crack in the mountain leads toward werewolves and a shining mercury pool. A second pool links the rocky island back to the crack. Finding a pool and successfully arriving through it are separate facts.

The island opens into steep tunnels and a snake pit. A tiny bone key opens the bone casket; the casket contains a different golden key for the wyrms’ treasure trapdoor. Opening a container does not prove that its contents were recovered.
The tiny bone key can break when used and cannot be rented. Prepare the return journey before entering dangerous tunnels; acquired keys, surviving a fall and a safe exit are different outcomes.
The great wyrms can call one another into a fight. Their armor, treasure and defeated bodies have distinct sources. A roar or recovered scale suit does not prove lasting protection for travelers.

Named relics have different wielding, class, alignment, speech and daily-use conditions. Owning one, activating it successfully and helping a beneficiary with its effect are separate facts. Some relics are stocked outside Mir.

The rune-covered stone in the wyrms’ vault follows its own touch and group reward rules. A stone visit or accepted epic award does not complete the priest’s scroll request or every wider forest story.

New tracking requires active READY accounting. Daily replay remains disabled until actual approach, usable source or supplied scroll, accepted experience and token, saved recipient history and legitimate renewed supply are qualified.

stories.title: Bring the fallen priest the light and dark scroll
stories.summary: Offer the exact scroll for experience and a satanic token. Source recovery, supplied custody, accepted reward and lasting forest outcomes are distinct.

steps.text: Carry the exact light and dark scroll loose
steps.hint: The male thorny worm carries the source scroll in a hidden dark hole. An exact supplied copy also fits. This optional row shows loose custody without proving a kill, first recovery or survived route.
